paper_metadata.title: Stereoelectroencephalography in the Presurgical Evaluation of Focal Epilepsy: A Retrospective Analysis of 215 Procedures

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a comprehensive description of a large, consecutive series of patients from a specialized center. Inclusion criteria are clearly defined based on specific clinical scenarios where non-invasive tests failed. Baseline characteristics (age, duration, seizure frequency) are well-reported.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: 211 patients (4 patients were explored twice), who showed variable patterns of localizing incoherence among electrical (interictal/ictal scalp electroencephalography), clinical (ictal semeiology), and anatomic (magnetic resonance imaging [MRI]) investigations.
items.reasoning: The target population is clearly defined as patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy requiring invasive monitoring due to discordant non-invasive findings.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: The aim of the present retrospective study was to report on indications, technical aspects, results, and morbidity of SEEG in a large consecutive series of patients.
items.reasoning: The study uses a consecutive series from a single specialized center, which is standard for this type of surgical prognosis study.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: During the 7-year period from 1996 through 2002
items.reasoning: The specific years of the study are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: "Claudio Munari" Center for Epilepsy Surgery, Ospedale Niguarda-Ca' Granda, Milan, Italy
items.reasoning: The specific clinical center and location are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: one of the following situations resulted from the noninvasive workup, thus indicating the need of invasive SEEG recording: 1) with no definite anatomic abnormality at MRI... 2) with a well-documented MRI abnormality, ictal/interictal scalp EEG findings and/or ictal clinical semeiology suggested a wide involvement also of extralesional areas...
items.reasoning: The authors list five specific clinical indications that served as inclusion criteria for the SEEG procedure.

items.evidence_snippet: The aim of the present retrospective study was to report on... a large consecutive series of patients.
items.reasoning: As a retrospective analysis of all consecutive procedures in the timeframe, participation bias is minimized.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: There were 120 males and 91 females, whose mean age at seizure onset was 7.8 - 6.7 years... mean age was 26.9 - 11.9 years... mean duration of epilepsy was 19.1 - 10.6 years... mean monthly seizure frequency was 59 -109 seizures
items.reasoning: Key demographic and clinical epilepsy characteristics are provided with means and ranges.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The flow of patients from SEEG to surgery and then to follow-up is meticulously documented. Only a small number of patients were lost to follow-up or excluded for clear clinical reasons (e.g., multifocal EZ).

items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: One-hundred-sixty-five patients have a postoperative follow-up period of at least 1 year, and the results of surgery on seizures are summarized in Table 8.
items.reasoning: Out of 174 operated patients, 165 (95%) provided follow-up data, which is a high retention rate.

items.reasoning: The reasons for not reaching surgery are described, but specific methods for tracking those lost after surgery are not detailed beyond the follow-up duration.
